items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: And when Harrison would get off to play, he'd say, Chris come get me. And he'd tell Chris to get me, come get me, you see. And I'd go play.

ctx.x: How many days you had steady you worked with Chris? Were you a member of Chris's band? Who me?

Who me? No, no, no. I never remember Chris's band. I always remember Chris's band like when someone played, Harrison Bourne was working over at, in the shop, moving out of here. In the shop with a well-tooled, with a bottle of tubes. And when Harrison would get off to play, he'd say, Chris come get me. And he'd tell Chris to get me, come get me, you see. And I'd go play. And Harrison was a welder, you see. He was a welder. Flu welder they call him. A man of a job like that, you know, good and well. He'd have been…
Let's see, I thought Sonny played with Chris for a while.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: I got with Harrison Bones, Yank and all them fellas, Buddy Johnson, Eddie Vincent and all them fellas, fast fellas, you see? And I used to pay attention to what they were doing, you see?

ctx.x: Well, who was the best trombone player then, Norfolk?

A real thunk trombone player, you know what I mean? Well, I tell you, at the time then, you see Dick, tell you the truth, them was more of a musical man, but good man, you understand? And they could play jazz too, you understand? But there was more musical man, you know? India was always good trombone players. Now they had to take like, they had Boris Fletcher right around there playing trombone. They had George Washington, Eddie Morris. Now all the people was playing more trombone when I was playing. They were…
Did you ever see any vowel trombone players?
